description: Single-panel secondary-electron SEM micrograph; imaging parameters printed at bottom left are "20kV X5,000 5µm", i.e. 20 kV accelerating voltage, ×5,000 magnification and a 5 µm scale bar. The field contains several large, smooth, essentially featureless grains separated by sharp boundaries, with only a few small isolated particles scattered in the grain interiors. A continuous, slightly brighter band with a raised, rib-like topographic appearance follows a roughly horizontal grain boundary across almost the entire width of the image; at the point where it meets a near-vertical boundary in the upper right it swells into an irregular bulge, so the boundary film forms a connected network with no visible gaps. The band is clearly narrower than the 5 µm scale-bar length. The caption identifies the structure as κ- and/or M3C carbides along γ grain boundaries in 9Al-20Mn-1C at 600 °C and claims "evidence of the continuity with grain"; the Greek phase symbols are missing from the supplied caption text, so the carbide types cannot be confirmed from the caption string alone. Taken as a whole the figure demonstrates that after exposure at 600 °C the carbides exist as a continuous grain-boundary film, continuous with the adjacent boundary, rather than as discrete isolated precipitates.

observations.observation: The image is a single SEM micrograph annotated with '20kV X5,000 5µm' at the bottom left, i.e. 20 kV accelerating voltage, ×5,000 magnification and a 5 µm scale bar.
A continuous brighter band runs along a roughly horizontal grain boundary from the left edge to the right edge of the field of view.
The boundary band thickens into an irregular bulge at the junction with a near-vertical boundary in the upper right, and the boundary film therefore forms a connected network without visible breaks.
The grain interiors are smooth and nearly featureless apart from a few small isolated particles; no lamellar or Widmanstätten structure is visible within the grains.
The grain-boundary band is markedly narrower than the 5 µm length of the printed scale bar.
No numeric composition, temperature or width values are printed on the image itself; the only text is the acceleration voltage, magnification and scale-bar label.
The caption states the figure shows κ- and/or M3C carbides along γ grain boundaries in 9Al-20Mn-1C at 600 °C.
The caption claims 'evidence of the continuity with grain', i.e. morphological continuity of the grain-boundary carbide with the adjacent grain/boundary.

The supplied caption string is corrupt/truncated: the Greek phase symbols before '-Carbides' and before 'grain boundaries' are missing, so the exact carbide types and the matrix phase symbol cannot be recovered from the caption text.
The figure body carries no panel letters (a)/(b), consistent with a single-image figure.
